title: Al2O3/MgF2 periodic Bragg stack with single defect cavity
scientific_hypothesis: Al2O3/MgF2 material pair provides better UV transparency than HfO2/SiO2 for 255-280 nm bandpass, achieving higher transmission with comparable blocking performance.
design_principle: MgF2 has exceptional UV transparency down to 200 nm and lower refractive index than SiO2. Al2O3 also maintains good UV transparency. The lower index contrast may require more layers but reduces absorption risk.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 17 layers (8 pairs + 1 cavity + 8 pairs)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 17, under 30-layer limit
Al2O3 and MgF2 are conventional e-beam depositable materials
MgF2 requires careful deposition to avoid porosity
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg reflectors
Defect mode theory for cavity resonance
UV material transparency data for Al2O3 and MgF2
expected_advantages: Superior UV transparency below 260 nm compared to HfO2
MgF2 has lowest refractive index among common UV materials
Lower absorption risk in solar-blind band
known_risks: Lower index contrast requires more layers for same blocking
MgF2 film stress and adhesion can be challenging
17 layers leaves less margin under 30-layer limit
execution_request_english: Design a defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 8 periods of Al2O3/MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) quarter-wave pairs, one Al2O3 cavity layer at center, then 8 periods of MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos)/Al2O3 quarter-wave pairs. Total 17 layers. Optimize all individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: al2o3, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos).
